summary: 38-year-old man with MLH1 Lynch syndrome, asymptomatic, last colonoscopy 3 years ago. BSG/ACPGBI/UKCGG 2020: 2-yearly colonoscopy from age 25 (MLH1/MSH2) — he is overdue; aspirin chemoprevention to be discussed.

inputs.hpi: Known Lynch syndrome (MLH1 pathogenic variant, found after his mother’s colorectal cancer at 44). Last colonoscopy 3 years ago: one 4 mm adenoma removed. No symptoms: no bleeding, bowels normal, weight steady. Not on aspirin.

imaging.name: Colonoscopy (3 years ago)
imaging.result: Complete to caecum, good preparation. 4 mm tubular adenoma, low-grade dysplasia, sigmoid — removed.

comorbidities: Family history of colorectal cancer (mother, age 44)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Lynch syndrome (MLH1) — surveillance colonoscopy overdue
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Lynch syndrome, MLH1 carrier. Surveillance colonoscopy overdue (last 3 years ago; 2-yearly interval).

guideline.name: BSG/ACPGBI/UKCGG guidelines — management of hereditary colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Lynch syndrome: 2-yearly colonoscopy from age 25 (MLH1, MSH2) or 35 (MSH6, PMS2); aspirin chemoprevention

rationale: Asymptomatic high-risk surveillance: the risk lives in the comorbidity list and the family history, not in symptoms. Tests whether any engine turns a Lynch diagnosis into a surveillance colonoscopy with the right interval.
